2022 Lexus LC 500 Owner Believes Their Car Is Worth More Than $87,500, What Say You?
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
After more than nine years in production, Lexus finally pulled the plug on the LC a few months ago, as the final copy rolled off the line in August 2026 at the Toyota City (Motomachi) factory in Japan.
Nevertheless, despite being old, this model hasn’t really started to show its age, has it? And for what it’s worth, it remains one of the best-looking premium grand tourers in the modern era. The average market price today spans from roughly $80,000 to over $100,000 in the United States of America. Some examples can reach up to $150,000, whereas others can drop below the $60,000 mark.
Paying in the region of $60K, sometimes less, would get you a Lexus LC from an early model year that has over 50,000 miles (80,000 km) on the odo. Later model years that have not seen that much action easily break into the six-digit territory . So, where does the pictured car fit? Well, it’s a 2022 model year that had 18,700 miles (30,100 km) under its belt at the time of cataloging, and that makes it an average example.
The vinyl exterior accents in the same tone as the cockpit may not be to everyone’s liking. This is an LC 500 Coupe, meaning that it packs a 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8. The engine produced 471 hp (477 ps/351 kW) and 398 pound-feet (540 Nm) of torque when the car was new, channeling everything to the rear wheels via a 10-speed automatic transmission. This model hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 4.4 seconds, and needed over 13 seconds to complete the standing quarter mile.
Photo: Cars&Bids Some of the gear mentioned in the listing includes the All-Weather Package, Bespoke Build Package, 21-inch wheels, carbon fiber roof, and adaptive variable suspension. This Lexus LC 500 Coupe also features a heated steering wheel, heated, ventilated, and power-adjustable front sports seats, a head-up display, and a premium surround sound system from Mark Levinson, among other things.
There is a crack in front of the right front wheel, another one in front of the left rear wheel, an it looks like this machine needs an evaporator core service, the listing reveals. It had its 20,000-mile (32,186 km) service performed in August 2026, and one year before, it had its engine oil and filter changed, an alignment performed, and the cabin air filter, wipers, and key battery replaced.
The seller bought it in January 2024, and they recently put it up for grabs on Cars&Bids. The online auction ended on November 18, 2026, and with the reserve not being met, this machine failed to sell. The highest bid was $87,500, and if you believe that this Lexus LC is worth more, and you actually want it, then you should reach out to the seller here on the quoted website.
